- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp historical spikes, then decay too slowly.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model fails to show sufficient downward correction after peaks.
- Late forecast days (last 5–10) often show underestimation, suggesting lagged or delayed response to recent price drops.
- When history includes a strong downward trend, model fails to fully reflect the trend’s persistence, leading to over-optimistic recovery forecasts.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture volatility clustering or sudden reversals in price direction.
- Model exhibits “anchoring bias” — tends to stick to recent high values even when data suggests a correction is imminent.
- In cases of prolonged price consolidation, model overreacts to minor fluctuations, creating artificial volatility in forecasts.
